prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (max 500 words)

Scope and funding
- Focus on Westminster decisions largely affecting England; separate approaches in devolved nations.
- Reallocate roughly £5bn/year from lower-priority programs: abolish a central industry department and subsidies; cancel ID cards; redirect Child Trust Fund to early-years class-size cuts.
- Introduce a 50% rate on income above £100,000 to fund: scrapping university tuition/top-up fees; free personal care for elderly/disabled people; lower local taxation.
- Replace Council Tax with a Local Income Tax collected via the existing system; typical household saving claimed at ~£450/year.

Health and social care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people.
- Faster diagnostics via expanded scanning capacity (including evenings/weekends), more community testing, and published diagnostic waits.
- End charges for eye/dental check-ups; widen prescription charge exemptions based on independent review.
- More frontline staff; reduce central targets; greater local accountability.
- Dental contract reform; personal care plans for long-term conditions; stronger palliative and mental health safeguards; end age discrimination.
- Prevention: school nutrition standards, restrict junk-food ads to children, ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition/top-up fees and restore maintenance grants.
- Use Child Trust Fund resources to hire ~21,000 teachers; infant classes to average 20, junior to 25; extend 8am–6pm provision; complete Children’s Centres.
- Ensure core subjects taught by qualified specialists; reduce high-stakes testing at 7 and 11 in favor of teacher assessment and sampling.
- Stronger special educational needs support; integrated academic–vocational 14–19 diplomas; modern college facilities; preserve school transport rights.

Crime, justice, and borders
- 10,000 extra police funded by cancelling ID cards; streamline police paperwork and tech.
- Emphasize tackling traffickers and acquisitive drug-related crime; community penalties for non-violent offenders with local input.
- Address binge drinking; extend late-night venue contributions to policing.
- Make prison days work/education-focused; link effort to release decisions.
- Establish a UK Border Force; prosecute terrorism in regular courts; repeal control-order laws; permit intercept evidence with judicial oversight.
- Single Equality Act; hate-crime units; transfer asylum decisions to a specialist agency; allow asylum seekers to work.

Economy, tax, and business
- Maintain fiscal rules with independent audit of budget figures and statistics.
- Raise stamp duty threshold to £150,000.
- Simplify regulation: impact assessments, sunset clauses, single inspections.
- Small business rate relief; reform to site-value rating; consumer “duty to trade fairly.”
- Tourism strategy and English Tourism Board.

Housing and local communities
- Release public land for ~100,000 affordable homes; VAT reforms to favor reuse and brownfield; planning permission for conversion to second homes in pressured areas.
- Restore Lottery independence; protect post offices; reduce overlapping inspections and central controls.

International, defence, and development
- Opposed the Iraq war; support stabilisation, inclusive politics, service restoration, and aim to withdraw troops with UN mandate expiry.
- Support EU reform and constitution via referendum; prepare for euro entry subject to tests.
- Defence: avoid overstretch; procurement reform; reallocate from lower-priority programs; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral reductions; tighter arms export oversight.
- Increase aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; fairer trade, end agricultural dumping; promote sustainable development (renewables, water, agriculture, biodiversity).

Rural, transport, and environment
- Fair dealing in food supply chains; CAP and fisheries reform; Marine Act; new animal welfare framework; caution on GM with labeling and GM-free zones option.
- Rail reform and targeted investment; expand congestion charging; VED reform to favor low-emission cars; long-term national road pricing; free off-peak buses for pensioners/disabled; greener aviation charges.
- Climate: meet Kyoto early; 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; carbon tax; no replacement of ageing nuclear stations; zero-waste goal with 60% household recycling in seven years.

Governance
- War Powers Act; Civil Service Act; strengthen parliamentary scrutiny; reduce ministers/departments; devolve powers; proportional voting (STV) for all elections and a predominantly elected second chamber; voting at the age of legal adulthood milestones; independent BBC regulator; Environmental Responsibility Act and green public procurement.
